Ingrid Morrow.narrative: I have mended nets on the Fish Steps for forty years, and from this bench I see every back that walks the quay. I raised Lark after the fever took my Siri, and I have watched the lamp at the mole fill her head with ships. She says she saw a sail last spring; I say the light plays tricks on a young eye. Magda Tarn hears what I see before anyone else does, and that is how the Strand keeps itself.
goals: Get Lark to stop talking about the sail and settle to the wrack and the net
Keep my bench on the Fish Steps and my place as the one who sees
See Lark safely grown and perhaps matched, before I am too old to watch her
pastimes: Mending a net in the sun and listening to the quay
Sitting at the wash-house wall in the evening
A slow walk up to the Crown to see the whole town below
Ingrid Morrow.calling: Net-mending is the work I love: a net well mended is a catch certain, and my bench is the best seat in Cullet.

relations.name: Lark Morrow
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: I raised her from a baby and love her, but I wish she would let the sail go.

relations.name: Magda Tarn
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She hears what I see before anyone else, and she divides the catch fair.

relations.name: Anselm Faro
relations.label: lamp keeper
relations.note: A good man, but his lamp keeps my girl's head full of ships.

relations.name: Amara Okoro
relations.label: fellow gatherer
relations.note: She gathers beside my Lark and brings her home safe.

relations.name: Hana Sato
relations.label: fellow gatherer
relations.note: Quiet and steady, and her husband's smoke lies on my washing.

relations.name: Greta Dunmore
relations.label: wash-house neighbour
relations.note: She hears everything at the wall, and I hear it from her.

relations.name: Petra Tarn
relations.label: smoker
relations.note: She buys my mended nets and smokes a good fish.

relations.name: Col Roon
relations.label: strand walker
relations.note: A polite lad who walks the strand when Lark does; I keep an eye on him.

relations.name: Livia Faro
relations.label: lamp house
relations.note: She renders the oil that keeps her uncle's light burning, and she talks with my Lark at the mole at dusk — the two of them fill the girl's head with ships between them.

memories.gist: The fever winter: I nursed Siri and could not save her, and then I took Lark into my house.
The storm last autumn took the end rail of the mole and half the slates off Low Row; I sat mending nets while the wind screamed.
My mother told me how her own mother remembered the last ship going out and the lean years after, when half the town went with it.
Lark came running to my bench last spring saying she had seen a sail beyond the Combs; I told her it was the light and the fog.
Magda Tarn first asked me to mend her house's nets when I was a young woman, and I have mended them ever since.

stances.why: I have watched that water forty years and never seen a ship; the lamp and the fog make shapes for a young eye.
Oil that could feed a family burns every night for ships that never come.
We came off the last ships together and we have only each other.
My bench has kept half the Strand fed, and I am not ashamed of it.

Lark Morrow.narrative: I gather kelp on the Wrack Strand with Amara and Hana, early, whatever the weather. Last spring at dusk I saw a sail beyond the Combs, pale against the Pale, for as long as it takes to say so. Nobody else saw it, and my grandmother says it was the light. I go to the tip of the mole every dusk to watch for it again.
goals: See the sail again and prove I saw it
Learn what lies beyond the Combs and the Pale
Keep my grandmother from worrying while I watch
pastimes: Standing at the tip of the mole at dusk, watching the water beyond the Combs
Gathering sea-glass on the Wrack Strand and sorting it by colour
Listening to Anselm Faro talk about the lamp and the old days
Lark Morrow.calling: I gather wrack because I must, but what I want is to go out past the Combs and see what is there.

relations.name: Ingrid Morrow
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She raised me and I love her, but she will not believe me about the sail.

relations.name: Amara Okoro
relations.label: fellow gatherer
relations.note: She gathers beside me and knows every colour of sea-glass.

relations.name: Hana Sato
relations.label: fellow gatherer
relations.note: Quiet and kind, and she listens when I talk about the sail.

relations.name: Anselm Faro
relations.label: lamp keeper
relations.note: He lights the Watchglass every dusk and never laughs at me for watching.

relations.name: Col Roon
relations.label: strand walker
relations.note: He walks the strand when I do and has not spoken to me yet.

relations.name: Livia Faro
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We talk at the mole at dusk while her uncle lights the lamp.

relations.name: Magda Tarn
relations.label: elder
relations.note: She divides the catch and my grandmother trusts her word.

memories.gist: Last spring at dusk I saw a sail beyond the Combs, pale against the Pale, for as long as it takes to say so.
The fever winter took my mother Siri; I was small, and my grandmother took me in.
Anselm Faro showed me how the Watchglass burns and told me the keepers' vow, and I have watched the light ever since.
Gathering kelp with Amara and Hana on a cold morning, and Amara showing me which wreck each colour of sea-glass came from.

stances.why: I know what I saw, and I will not be talked out of it.
The Watchglass burns every night until the ships come back; the sail is a sign they are coming.
If a ship can pass them, so can something built here.
My grandmother taught me that, and I believe it even when I want to leave.
